Package com.kerosene.kfe.bootstrap.config.persistence

Class KfeStringColumnCryptoService

java.lang.Object
com.kerosene.kfe.bootstrap.config.persistence.KfeStringColumnCryptoService
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.kerosene.common.security.StringColumnCryptoPort
@Service public class KfeStringColumnCryptoService extends Object implements com.kerosene.common.security.StringColumnCryptoPort
AES-256-GCM column crypto for KFE standalone (xpub/descriptor at rest).

The main auth server uses CosignerSecretService + Vault. KFE is a separate process and only scans com.kerosene.kfe, so it needs its own port or StringCryptoConverter fails with "crypto port is not initialized".

Key resolution (first match):

  1. KFE_COLUMN_CRYPTO_KEY_BASE64 — primary 32-byte AES key, base64
  2. SHA-256 of KFE_INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET — only if kfe.crypto.allow-shared-secret-derivation=true (off by default)

Key rotation: set KFE_COLUMN_CRYPTO_KEY_BASE64_V2 to a new key. Decrypt tries v1 then v2; encrypt always uses the highest available version.

  • Constructor Details

    • KfeStringColumnCryptoService

      public KfeStringColumnCryptoService(@Value("${kfe.column-crypto.key-base64:}") String keyBase64, @Value("${kfe.column-crypto.key-base64-v2:}") String keyBase64V2, @Value("${kfe.internal.shared-secret:}") String sharedSecret, @Value("${kfe.crypto.allow-shared-secret-derivation:false}") boolean allowSharedSecretDerivation)
      Resolves the active encryption key and retained decryption keys from configuration. A dedicated base64 256-bit key is preferred; deriving from the internal shared secret requires an explicit opt-in and emits a warning because it couples authentication and data keys.
      Parameters:
      keyBase64 - primary dedicated AES-256 key, if configured
      keyBase64V2 - optional rotation key written by new encryption operations
      sharedSecret - source for the compatibility derivation fallback
      allowSharedSecretDerivation - whether the fallback key derivation is explicitly enabled
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no permitted key source is configured or a key is invalid

  • Method Details

    • encrypt

      public com.kerosene.common.security.EncryptedValue encrypt(com.kerosene.common.security.CryptoPurpose purpose, byte[] plaintext, byte[] associatedData)
      Encrypts plaintext with purpose-bound AES-GCM and returns separately represented ciphertext/tag. A fresh random nonce is generated for every call; purpose and nonempty associated data are authenticated with a versioned domain prefix, so ciphertext cannot be reused across contexts.
      Specified by:
      encrypt in interface com.kerosene.common.security.StringColumnCryptoPort
      Parameters:
      purpose - semantic use that is bound into the authentication data
      plaintext - bytes to encrypt
      associatedData - nonempty record/context identity authenticated but not encrypted
      Returns:
      encrypted payload, key identifier, algorithm metadata, nonce, tag, and creation time
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if required values are null or associated data is empty
      IllegalStateException - if the cryptographic provider fails

    • decrypt

      public byte[] decrypt(com.kerosene.common.security.CryptoPurpose purpose, com.kerosene.common.security.EncryptedValue encrypted, byte[] associatedData)
      Decrypts a purpose-bound AES-GCM value using the key identified by its stable key ID. Authentication failure, wrong purpose/context, and unavailable key IDs fail closed.
      Specified by:
      decrypt in interface com.kerosene.common.security.StringColumnCryptoPort
      Parameters:
      purpose - expected semantic use bound when the value was encrypted
      encrypted - metadata and ciphertext to authenticate and decrypt
      associatedData - nonempty record/context identity used during encryption
      Returns:
      original plaintext bytes after successful GCM authentication
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for missing context or unsupported format metadata
      IllegalStateException - when the key is unavailable or authenticated decryption fails
